questions.stem: How can research serve its full purpose according to the author?

analysis.label: 判型
analysis.text: How can research serve its full purpose according to the author? 问的是"通过什么方 式"，要求从文中找到作者明示的条件句。

analysis.label: 拆句
analysis.text: 题干 How can research serve its full purpose according to the author? 是一个标准 How 类疑问句：情态动词 can 提到主语 research 前，谓语 serve 带宾语 its full purpose；according to the author 是状语，只是限定信息来源，不影响理解。结构平铺 直叙，无陷阱。

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: For research to serve its full purpose, the results must leave the confines of research laboratories and academic journals. 要让研究充分发挥其作用，研究结果必须走出实验室和学术期刊的范围。 46. How can research serve its full purpose according to the author? A) With researchers being aware of public interests. B) With its findings published in prominent journals. C) With researchers creating products that enhance social development. D) With its findings properly communicated beyond the academic circle.

analysis.label: 选项
analysis.text: A) 无中生有 With researchers being aware of public interests 说"研究者要意识到公众利益"，原 文从未谈论"研究者的觉察"这一前提，P1 强调的是"传播"而非"觉察"。 B) 与原文相反 With its findings published in prominent journals 把"发表在顶级期刊上"当作答案， 但 P1 恰恰指出"必须离开学术期刊"——发表在顶级期刊只是 P4 中讲到的研究者评职称 的手段，与"研究发挥充分作用"相反。 C) 张冠李戴 With researchers creating products that enhance social development 把 creating products and innovations that enhance development 这句"研究的目标之一"挪用来 作为"研究发挥作用的方式"——这是研究的目的描述，不是 serve its full purpose 的 条件。 D) ✓ 正确 the results must leave the confines of research laboratories and academic journals ↔ With its findings properly communicated beyond the academic circle 选项 With its findings properly communicated beyond the academic circle 用同义 替换还原了预判的"研究结果必须走出学术圈"，是定位句的标准转述。 为什么普通读者难以获取研究人员的研究结果? A) 他们无法理解报告这些结果时使用的学术语言 B) 他们对研究人员用来描述其发现的术语感到畏惧 C) 他们不参加可以免费获取这些结果的会议 D) 他们几乎没有机会找到发表这些研究成果的期刊

analysis.text: 题干 Why do ordinary readers find it difficult to access the results of researchers' studies? 主干是 readers find it difficult to access，find sth difficult to do 是常见结 构，it 是形式宾语，真正宾语是后面的不定式 to access...；the results of researchers' studies 是多重 of 修饰的名词短语。无难点。

analysis.label: 选项

questions.stem: What is one of the reasons some researchers won't prioritise communicating their findings to the public?

analysis.label: 判型
analysis.text: What is one of the reasons some researchers won't prioritise communicating their findings to the public? 直接问"原因之一"，要求从原文找明示因果句。

analysis.label: 拆句
analysis.text: 题干 What is one of the reasons some researchers won't prioritise communicating their findings to the public? 主干是 What is one of the reasons...；reasons 后的 some researchers won't prioritise... 是省略 that 的定语从句修饰 reasons；communicating 后 的 their findings to the public 是 V-ing 短语的双宾语结构。结构略长但语义清晰。 48. What is one of the reasons some researchers won't prioritise communicating their findings to the public? A) They can thrive on the papers published. B) Their top consideration is to win tenure C) Their main goal is gaining recognition in their field. D) They have to struggle to reach out to the community.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: For researchers in the tenure-track system, their main goal is winning tenure, which in part can be achieved by getting a number of papers published in prominent journals. Pressures like this mean community-level outreach is not prioritised. 对处在终身教职轨制度中的研究者来说，他们的主要目标是获得终身教职，而获得终身教职 部分可以通过在顶级期刊上发表若干论文实现。诸如此类的压力意味着面向社区层面的对外 传播不被优先考虑。

analysis.label: 选项
analysis.text: A) 答非所问 They can thrive on the papers published 说"他们靠发表的论文茁壮成长"——题干问 的是"为什么不优先对外传播的原因"，A 描述的是"发文的结果/好处"，而非"不愿对外传 播的原因"，且 thrive on 的积极语义与原文"压力"对应不上。 B) ✓ 正确 their main goal is winning tenure ↔Their top consideration is to win tenure 选项 Their top consideration is to win tenure 是定位句 their main goal is winning tenure 几乎逐词的同义替换，且与预判"首要目标是 tenure"完全一致。 C) 无中生有 Their main goal is gaining recognition in their field 把研究者目标改成"在领域内获 得认可"——原文 their main goal is winning tenure 明确写的是 winning tenure（拿 到终身教职），不是 recognition；这是把因果中段的"靠发文"过度泛化为"求认可"。 D) 与原文相反 They have to struggle to reach out to the community 说"他们必须努力对外传播"， 但原文 community-level outreach is not prioritised 是说"不优先做"——不是"努力 做"，方向完全相反。 分享研究成果如何使研究人员自身受益? A) 帮助他们确定新的研究方向 B) 使他们能够理解困扰社会的危机 C) 使他们能够有效解决社会差异 D) 帮助他们与政府机构建立联系

questions.stem: How can sharing findings benefit researchers themselves?

analysis.label: 判型
analysis.text: How can sharing findings benefit researchers themselves? 问"如何受益"，需要在原文 找具体受益机制的陈述。

analysis.label: 拆句
analysis.text: 题干 How can sharing findings benefit researchers themselves? 主干 sharing findings 作主语（动名词短语），benefit 是及物动词，researchers themselves 是宾语+反身代词 强调。themselves 是理解关键，标明"受益方是研究者自己"。 49. How can sharing findings benefit researchers themselves? A) By helping them to identify new research directions. B) By enabling them to understand crises plaguing society. C) By enabling them to effectively address social discrepancies. D) By helping them to forge ties with government agencies.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Engaging with other researchers and the public can lead to unexpected new connections and new ideas that could suggest fruitful new directions for research. 与其他研究者及公众的互动可能催生意想不到的新联系和新想法，进而可能指明富有成果的 新研究方向。

analysis.label: 选项
analysis.text: A) ✓ 正确 could suggest fruitful new directions for research ↔ By helping them to identify new research directions 选项 By helping them to identify new research directions 是定位句 could suggest fruitful new directions for research 的同义改写，且 By Ving 结构正好回应题 干 How。 B) 张冠李戴 By enabling them to understand crises plaguing society 借用了 respond to crises that plague society 的措辞——但 P6 讲的是"分享有助于其他主体（家庭、社区、政 策制定者等）理解危机"，受益者并非"研究者自身"；与题干 researchers themselves 错位。 C) 张冠李戴 By enabling them to effectively address social discrepancies 借用 addressing certain social discrepancies 的措辞——同样是 P6 讲对社会的好处，而非对研究者自 身的好处；与题干 themselves 错位。 D) 无中生有 By helping them to forge ties with government agencies 说"帮助他们与政府机构建 立关系"——原文虽提过 government agencies（P6 列举受益方时），但从未把"与政 府机构结盟"作为研究者自身的受益方式。 为什么建议研究人员聘请专业作家或传播官员的服务? A) 满足伦理委员会对研究人员的强制性要求 B) 将他们的研究翻译成海外读者可理解的语言 C) 使他们的出版物被公众正确理解 D) 使他们的研究成果被知名期刊接受

analysis.label: 判型
analysis.text: Why are researchers advised to engage the services of professional writers or communication officers? 问"为何建议聘请"，需要从原文找明示的目的或结果状语。 50. Why are researchers advised to engage the services of professional writers or communication officers? A) To satisfy ethics committees' mandatory requirements of researchers. B) To translate their study into languages accessible to readers overseas. C) To make their publications correctly understood by the public. D) To render their findings acceptable by prominent journals.

analysis.label: 拆句
analysis.text: 题干 Why are researchers advised to engage the services of professional writers or communication officers? 是被动语态：are advised to do（被建议做）；engage 在此为 正式词义"聘请"；professional writers or communication officers 是并列名词词组。结构 清晰，注意 engage 不是"参与"而是"聘用"。

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: But this can be resolved by researchers engaging the services of professional writers or communication officers to help with translating their study into more accessible language and share it widely with media outlets and the public. 但这可以通过研究者聘请专业写手或传播官来解决，让他们帮助把研究"翻译"成更通俗易懂 的语言，并广泛地向媒体和公众分享。

analysis.label: 选项
analysis.text: A) 张冠李戴 To satisfy ethics committees' mandatory requirements of researchers 把 ethics committees should make it mandatory 这一伦理委员会的强制要求挪用来作为聘请 写手的目的；但 P10 与 P11 是两个独立建议——伦理委员会强制研究者分享是一回 事，聘请写手帮助翻译是另一回事，两者目的不同。 B) 偷换概念 To translate their study into languages accessible to readers overseas 把 more accessible language 偷换为 languages accessible to readers overseas（让海外读者 读懂）——原文从未提及 overseas / readers abroad 等概念，只说"通俗易懂"，不涉 及外语翻译。 C) ✓ 正确 to help with translating their study into more accessible language ↔ To make their publications correctly understood by the public There could be misunderstanding of the findings presented by the researcher because of technical terms. ↔correctly understood by the public 选项 To make their publications correctly understood by the public 是 P11 整段问 题（误解）与解决（翻译成通俗语言）的目的合成，与预判完全吻合。 D) 与原文相反 To render their findings acceptable by prominent journals 说"让顶级期刊接受研 究"——这是 P4 中谈到的另一动机（评 tenure 时投顶级期刊），且 P1 明确批判"留在 期刊里就发挥不了作用"；聘请写手的目的恰恰是"走出期刊面向公众"，方向相反。

questions.stem: What do we learn about spiders in the UK since the middle ages?

analysis.label: 判型
analysis.text: What do we learn about spiders in the UK since the middle ages? 用 What do we learn about 引出，问的是关于某对象的客观事实，没有 infer/imply/suggest 等推断信号

analysis.label: 拆句

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: But they are a constant source of human anxieties—with a cultural association with witches and wickedness dating back to the middle ages. 但它们一直是人类焦虑的来源——与女巫和邪恶的文化关联可追溯至中世纪。

analysis.label: 选项
analysis.text: A) ✓ 正确 a cultural association with witches and wickedness ↔generally misconceived its prevalence appears unrelated to any rational assessment of risk ↔misconceived 预判落在蜘蛛被文化误解上，A They have been generally misconceived 用 misconceived 概括了原文女巫、邪恶等不实联想，与预判完全对应，是定位句的高度抽 象同义替换。 B) 与原文相反 B 选项 They have adversely impacted crop growth 称蜘蛛对农作物生长有不利影 响，但原文 Farmland species perform valuable ecosystem services, by preying on insects that are our competitors for crops 明确说农田蜘蛛吃掉与人类争粮的昆虫， 是有利的；B 把有利说成有害，与原文相反。 C) 偷换概念 C 选项 They have been a constant reminder of bad luck 说蜘蛛是坏运气的提醒，但 原文说的是与女巫、邪恶（witches and wickedness）的文化关联， witches/wickedness 是邪恶/巫术，不等于坏运气（bad luck）；二者是不同的文化概 念，C 偷换了概念。 D) 答非所问 D 选项 They have made their presence felt when spinning webs 取自首段 Spiders make their presence felt in late August and through early autumn，讲的是晚夏初 秋的自然现象，与题干 since the middle ages 的时间范围毫无关系；属答非所问。 51. analysis.text: What have spiders been associated with in the UK for centuries? 用 What 引出过去完 成时的事实问句，问的是被关联的对象，没有任何推断信号

analysis.label: 拆句
analysis.text: 题干主干是 What have spiders been associated with，spiders 为主语，谓语为现在完成 时被动 have been associated with，介词 with 后的宾语正是要回答的内容；in the UK 是 地点状语，for centuries 是时间状语，结构清晰。

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: But they are a constant source of human anxieties—with a cultural association with witches and wickedness dating back to the middle ages. 但它们一直是人类焦虑的来源——与女巫和邪恶的文化关联可追溯至中世纪。

analysis.label: 选项
analysis.text: A) 偷换概念 A Harm 意为有形的伤害，对应原文应是 spiders 对人造成的实质损害；但原文 Spiders in the UK are almost all harmless 明确说英国蜘蛛几乎都无害——蜘蛛被关 联的是文化上的邪恶，而不是实际伤害；A 偷换概念。 B) ✓ 正确 wickedness ↔Evil witches ↔Evil 由预判 与巫术与邪恶相关联，选项 B Evil 把 witches 与 wickedness 两个并列宾语用一 个上位词 Evil 同时归纳，是定位句的精准同义替换。 C) 张冠李戴 C Suffering 指痛苦/折磨，原文 Fear of spiders is common and has serious impacts on the lives of sufferers 出现 sufferers 一词——但 sufferers 描述的是怕蜘蛛的人所 承受的影响，而题干问蜘蛛被关联的对象，主体错位；C 张冠李戴。 D) 无中生有 D Aggression 指攻击性，原文从未把蜘蛛与攻击性联系起来——焦虑、恐惧、邪恶都 不等于攻击；这是文中没有的概念，属无中生有。 52. questions.stem: What partly accounts for the reduction in spiders' food supply?

analysis.label: 判型
analysis.text: What partly accounts for the reduction in spiders' food supply? 用 What accounts for 直接问原因，是典型的因果型细节题，不是推断

analysis.label: 拆句
analysis.text: 题干主干是 What partly accounts for X，partly 修饰 accounts for，X 为名词短语 the reduction in spiders' food supply，其中 spiders' 是所有格修饰 food supply；句子结构 简单，重点是 partly 这一限定词。

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: A recent landmark study identified a 75% fall in insect populations between 1989 and 2016, with pesticide use thought to be to blame along with the destruction of wild areas for development. 近期一项标志性研究发现，1989 到 2016 年间昆虫种群下降了 75%，元凶是杀虫剂使用以 及为开发而破坏野生区域。 53. What partly accounts for the reduction in spiders' food supply? A) The long tradition of collecting insects. B) Fast reproduction of their competitors. C) Chemicals used for killing insects. A) You may have heard that learning another language is one method for preventing or at least postponing the onset of dementia. Dementia refers to the loss of cognitive abilities, and one of its most common forms is Alzheimer's disease(阿尔茨海默氏病). At this time, the causes of the disease are not well understood, and consequently, there are no proven steps that people can take to prevent it. Nonetheless, some researchers have suggested that learning a foreign language might help delay the onset of dementia.
B) To explore this possibility more deeply, let's look at some of the common misconceptions about dementia and the aging brain. First of all, dementia is not an inevitable part of the normal aging process. Most older adults do not develop Alzheimer's disease or other forms of dementia. It is also important to remember that dementia is not the same thing as normal forgetfulness. At any age, we might experience difficulty finding the exact word we want or have trouble remembering the name of the person we just met. People with dementia have more serious problems, like feeling confused or getting lost in a familiar place. Think of it this way: If you forget where you parked your car at the mall, that's normal; if you forget how to drive a car, that may be a signal that something more serious is going on.
C) The idea that dementia can be prevented is based on the comparison of the brain to a muscle. When people talk about the brain, they sometimes say things like "It is important to exercise your brain" or "To stay mentally fit, you have to give your brain a workout." Although these are colorful analogies, in reality the brain is not a muscle. Unlike muscles, the brain is always active and works even during periods of rest and sleep. In addition, although some muscle cells have a lifespan of only a few days, brain cells last a lifetime. Not only that, but it has been shown that new brain cells are being created throughout one's lifespan.
D) While it makes for a colorful analogy, comparing the brain to a muscle is inaccurate and misleading. So, if the brain is not a muscle, can it still be exercised? Once again, researchers don't know for sure. There are now many computer, online, and mobile device applications that claim to be able to "train your brain," and they typically tap into a variety of cognitive abilities. However, research suggests that although this type of training may improve one's abilities at the tasks themselves, they don't seem to improve other abilities. In other words, practicing a letter-detection task will, over time, improve your letter-detection skills, but it will not necessarily enhance your other perceptual abilities.
E) However, there is some reason to believe that learning languages might be different. The best evidence that foreign language learning confers cognitive benefits comes from research with those who are already bilingual(双语的). Bilingualism most commonly occurs when children are exposed to two languages, either in the home (mom speaks Dutch, dad speaks Spanish) or more formally in early schooling. But bilingualism certainly occurs in adulthood as well.
F) Bilingualism and multilingualism are actually more common than you might think. In fact, it has been estimated that there are fewer monolingual speakers in the world than bilinguals and multilinguals. Although in many countries most inhabitants share just one language, other countries have several official languages. Switzerland, for example, has four official languages: German, French, Italian, and Romansh. Throughout large parts of Africa, Arabic, Swahili, French, and English are often known and used by individuals who speak a different, native language in their home than they do in the marketplace. So bilingualism and multilingualism are to be found throughout the world. And with regard to cognitive abilities, the research on those who speak more than one language paints an encouraging picture.
G) For one thing, bilinguals are better at multitasking. One explanation of this superiority is that speakers of two languages are continually inhibiting one of their languages, and this process of inhibition confers general cognitive benefits to other activities. In fact, bilingual individuals outperform their monolingual counterparts on a variety of cognitive tasks, such as following complex instructions, and switching to new instructions. For the sake of completeness, it should be noted that the advantages of being bilingual are not universal across all cognitive domains. Bilingual individuals have been shown to have smaller vocabularies and to take longer in retrieving words from memory when compared to monolinguals. In the long run, however, the cognitive and linguistic advantages of being bilingual far outweigh these two drawbacks.
H) If the benefits of being bilingual spill over to other aspects of cognition, then we would expect to see a lower incidence of Alzheimer's disease in bilinguals than in monolinguals, or at least a later onset of Alzheimer's for bilinguals. In fact, there is evidence to support this claim. The psychologist Ellen Bialystok and her colleagues obtained the histories of 184 individuals who had made use of a memory clinic in Toronto. For those who showed signs of dementia, the monolinguals in the sample had an average age of 71.4 years at time of onset. The bilinguals, in contrast, received their diagnosis at 75.5 years, on average. In a study of this sort, a difference of four years is highly significant, and could not be explained by other systematic differences between the two groups. For example, the monolinguals reported, on average, a year and a half more schooling than their bilingual counterparts, so the effect was clearly not due to formal education.
I) A separate study, conducted in India, found strikingly similar results: bilingual patients developed symptoms of dementia 4.5 years later than monolinguals, even after other potential factors, such as gender and occupation, were controlled for. In addition, researchers have reported other positive effects of bilingualism for cognitive abilities in later life, even when the person acquired the language in adulthood. Crucially, Bialystok suggested that the positive benefits of being bilingual were only found in those who used both languages all the time.
J) But encouraging as these kinds of studies are, they still have not established exactly how or why differences between bilinguals and monolinguals exist. Because these studies looked back at the histories of people who were already bilingual, the results can only say that a difference between the two groups was found, but not why that difference occurred. Further research is needed to determine what caused the differences in age of onset between the two groups.
K) Other studies of successful aging suggest that being connected to one's community and having plenty of social interaction is also important in delaying or even preventing the onset of dementia. Once again, however, the results are far less clear than the popular media might lead you to believe. Older individuals who lead active social lives are, almost by definition, healthier than their counterparts who rarely leave their homes or interact with others. So we can't really say whether being socially active prevents the onset of dementia, or if people who don't have dementia are more likely to be socially active.
L) But even if studying a foreign language is not a magical cure-all, there is one thing it will do: It will make you a better speaker of a foreign language. Doing that confers a whole host of advantages we do know about.

reading-1.raw:
P1 Research is meant to benefit society by raising public awareness and creating products and innovations that enhance development. For research to serve its full purpose, the results must leave the confines of research laboratories and academic journals.

P2 Findings effectively communicated can go a long way to serve the interests of the public. They can help address social injustices or improve treatments offered to patients.

P3 Many researchers seem to be content with sharing the results of their studies in academic journals or at conferences. But few journals allow everybody to read the findings. Even articles freely available are usually written in academic language incomprehensible to the average reader.

P4 For researchers in the tenure-track system, their main goal is winning tenure, which in part can be achieved by getting a number of papers published in prominent journals. Pressures like this mean community-level outreach is not prioritised.

P5 Many researchers lack the writing skills to describe their results to a general audience. They may also worry about whether the public will understand their findings, or about findings being used to influence controversial policies. These concerns cause some researchers to shy away from communicating their findings outside the academic community.

P6 Propagating research findings beyond academic publications is particularly crucial for addressing certain social discrepancies. It can help families, communities, healthcare providers, policymakers, government agencies and other stakeholders to understand and respond to crises that plague society.

P7 The benefits of sharing findings flow both ways. Engaging with other researchers and the public can lead to unexpected new connections and new ideas that could suggest fruitful new directions for research.

P8 To benefit both researchers and the communities, the need to find innovative, accessible ways to share the work cannot be overstated.

P9 Institutions and funding organisations should support more researchers to publish in open access journals so that the public doesn't have to pay to read them. Institutions and researchers should invest in partnerships that expand capacity for sharing results more broadly.

P10 Furthermore, ethics committees should make it mandatory for researchers to share their results with the public. Every research participant should opt in or out of receiving results, as part of the process of giving informed consent.

P11 There could be misunderstanding of the findings presented by the researcher because of technical terms. But this can be resolved by researchers engaging the services of professional writers or communication officers to help with translating their study into more accessible language and share it widely with media outlets and the public.

P12 Sharing results with the people who are most affected by them makes us better researchers and ensures that our work can be used to improve people's lives. Institutions and collaborators must recognise the value of doing so.

blocks.text: Propagating research findings beyond academic publications is particularly crucial for addressing certain social discrepancies. It can help families, communities, healthcare providers, policymakers, government agencies and other stakeholders to understand and respond to crises that plague society.

blocks.label: P7
blocks.text: The benefits of sharing findings flow both ways. Engaging with other researchers and the public can lead to unexpected new connections and new ideas that could suggest fruitful new directions for research.

blocks.label: P8
blocks.text: To benefit both researchers and the communities, the need to find innovative, accessible ways to share the work cannot be overstated.

blocks.label: P9
blocks.text: Institutions and funding organisations should support more researchers to publish in open access journals so that the public doesn't have to pay to read them. Institutions and researchers should invest in partnerships that expand capacity for sharing results more broadly.

blocks.label: P10
blocks.text: Furthermore, ethics committees should make it mandatory for researchers to share their results with the public. Every research participant should opt in or out of receiving results, as part of the process of giving informed consent.

blocks.label: P11
blocks.text: There could be misunderstanding of the findings presented by the researcher because of technical terms. But this can be resolved by researchers engaging the services of professional writers or communication officers to help with translating their study into more accessible language and share it widely with media outlets and the public.

blocks.label: P12
blocks.text: Sharing results with the people who are most affected by them makes us better researchers and ensures that our work can be used to improve people's lives. Institutions and collaborators must recognise the value of doing so.

P1 Spiders make their presence felt in late August and through early autumn. This is the mating season of some of the most common varieties, when male house spiders come out of hidden corners to look for females, and garden spiders reach adult size and spin their most dazzling webs.

P2 Yet while the spider is a familiar fixture of nursery poems or songs and Halloween decorations, its relationship with humans is complicated. Fear of spiders is common and has serious impacts on the lives of sufferers. Its prevalence appears unrelated to any rational assessment of risk. Spiders in the UK are almost all harmless. Farmland species perform valuable ecosystem services, by preying on insects that are our competitors for crops. But they are a constant source of human anxieties—with a cultural association with witches and wickedness dating back to the middle ages.

P3 Does this perhaps explain, in part, the lack of data about how spiders are faring in our age of ecological crisis? British butterflies are the most studied group of insects in the world, due to the long tradition of collecting and observing them. But spider conservationists point out that it was only in the 1980s that the classification of house spiders was properly sorted out. And while information about insect populations is gathered by experiments that measure the numbers hitting windscreens or traps, there have been few attempts to count spiders.

P4 The huge reductions in the numbers of flying insects can only mean a reduction in spiders' food supply. A recent landmark study identified a 75% fall in insect populations between 1989 and 2016, with pesticide use thought to be to blame along with the destruction of wild areas for development. This means the overall picture for spiders is worrying, as it is for most creatures. But conservationists are most concerned about those varieties that are threatened due to habitat loss and fragmentation, which makes it impossible for them to migrate.

P5 Of around 650 spider species regularly recorded in the UK, the majority thrive in marshes and wasteland. Conservation efforts, often led by determined individuals, have helped some species to recover by reintroducing them to new areas. With rewilding now firmly on the environmental policy agenda, the hope is that in future, spiders will be enabled to migrate by themselves, adapting to climate change by moving along wildlife corridors.

P6 It seems unlikely that spiders will ever attract the same level of human enthusiasm as bees, birds or butterflies, in spite of their unique status as nature's spinners. But as they reveal themselves in all their splendour this autumn, it would be a good thing if more animal lovers recognised the ways in which spiders are simply terrific.

writing.directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence “With their valuable skills and experience, elderly people can continue to make significant contributions to society." You can make comments, cite examples or use your personal experiences to develop your essay. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
writing.model: With their valuable skills and experience, elderly people can continue to make significant contributions to society. Far from being a burden, seniors possess a lifetime of professional knowledge and practical wisdom that younger generations simply have not had time to acquire. This potential shows itself in countless ways. Take retired engineers and doctors as an example: many of them return to their former posts as consultants, training newcomers and solving problems that puzzle less experienced staff. In my own community, retired teachers volunteer to run free evening classes, while elderly craftsmen pass down traditional skills that would otherwise disappear. Such efforts prove that age brings not decline but a rich resource waiting to be tapped. Therefore, we should stop regarding old age merely as a time of rest and instead recognize its true worth. If society creates more opportunities for the elderly to share their expertise, everyone benefits. Only by valuing and drawing on their skills and experience can we build a wiser and more harmonious community.

In response, the Chinese government is taking various measures to promote the development of the elderly care service system, so that the elderly can enjoy a healthy and happy life in their later years. To improve the service quality of these institutions, the government has issued a series of standards, strengthening the supervision of them. translation.reference: In recent years, the elderly population in China has been growing continuously. In response, the Chinese government is taking various measures to promote the development of the elderly care service system, so that the elderly can enjoy a healthy and happy life in their later years. Various elderly care institutions have been built across the country. To improve the service quality of these institutions, the government has issued a series of standards, strengthening the supervision of them. To make dining more convenient for the elderly, many cities have opened community canteens, which provide affordable meals for them. In addition, elderly people with limited mobility can also enjoy home meal delivery services. At the same time, China is also actively exploring other elderly care models, such as home-based and community-based care, to ensure that all the elderly are well cared for in their old age.

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 老龄人口（主语）+ 增长（谓语）（主语策略：原句主语） 中文已有明确主语 中国老龄人口，直接作英文主语 the elderly population in China；核心动词是 持续增长，作谓语 has been growing / continues to grow。主干即「人口 + 在增长」。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 时间状语前置 + 副词修饰动词 本句结构简单，几乎无需降级。只把 近年来 处理成时间状语 in recent years 放句首，持续 这一 「持续地」的意思用 has been growing 的进行体或 continuously 副词体现，不必单独成句。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 「近年来 + 持续增长」表示从过去延续到现在并仍在继续，最贴的是现在完成进行时 has been growing；若拿不准，用一般现在时 continues to grow 也对，但不要用一般过去时 grew（那会 变成「过去增长过、现在不增了」，与原意相反）。 主谓一致 主语 the elderly population 是单数（population 作整体），谓语动词用单数 has / continues， 不要写成 have / continue。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: In recent years, the elderly population in China has been growing continuously. 2. 中国政府正采取各种措施，推进养老服务体系建设，使老年人晚年生活健康幸福。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 政府（主语）+ 采取（谓语）+ 措施（宾语）（主语策略：原句主语） 主语是 中国政府 → the Chinese government；最核心的动作是 采取各种措施，作主谓宾 is taking various measures。后面「推进……」「使……」都是采取措施要达到的目的，不与「采 取」并列作谓语。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 两个「目的」降级为不定式 推进养老服务体系建设 是采取措施的目的 降级为 to promote the development of the elderly care service system；使老年人晚年生活健康幸福 是更远的目的 用 so that 从句或 to ensure 接出来：so that the elderly can enjoy a healthy and happy life in their later years。 这样三个中文动词被理顺成「谓语 + 目的 + 目的」的层级，而非流水句。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 正采取 的「正」表此刻进行，用现在进行时 is taking，在全篇一般现在时基调上的合理偏离。 单复数 各种措施 是多种，measures 用复数；the elderly 作复数群体，后面用 can enjoy 复数动词。 用词 「晚年生活」译 their later years / their old age 即可，不必逐字译「生活 life」再加 in old age，避免啰嗦。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: The Chinese government is taking various measures to promote the development of the elderly care service system, so that the elderly can enjoy a healthy and happy life in their later years. 3. 全国兴建了各类养老服务机构。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 各类养老服务机构（受动者作主语）+ 被兴建（主语策略：转被动） 中文 全国兴建了各类养老服务机构 是无明确施动者的无主句（「全国」是地点不是真正主语）， 动作的承受者是「机构」。把承受者提作主语转被动：Various elderly care institutions have been built across the country。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 「全国」降级为地点状语 全国 不作主语，降级为地点状语 across the country / nationwide 放句末。各类 作定语 various / all kinds of 修饰 institutions。本句结构短，转被动后即成。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态语态 兴建了 的「了」表已完成且机构现仍在，用现在完成时被动 have been built；这是相对全篇一般 现在时的合理偏离。 单复数 各类 机构不止一类一所，institutions 用复数，对应助动词用 have been。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: Various elderly care institutions have been built across the country. 4. 为了提升养老机构的服务质量，政府颁布了一系列标准，加强对养老机构的监管。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 政府（主语）+ 颁布（谓语）+ 一系列标准（宾语）（主语策略：原句主语） 主干是 政府颁布了一系列标准 → the government has issued a series of standards。为了提 升……服务质量 是目的状语，加强对养老机构的监管 是颁布标准带来的结果/并列动作，均不作主 干谓语。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 目的状语前置 + 结果用现在分词 为了提升养老机构的服务质量 不定式短语 To improve the service quality of elderly care institutions 置于句首作目的状语；加强对养老机构的监管 是颁布标准自然带来的结果，降级为现 在分词状语 strengthening the supervision of these institutions 挂在主句后，避免再起一个 and 平句。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 颁布了 表已完成且标准现行有效，用现在完成时 has issued；与第3句同理，是基调的合理偏离。 指代 第二次出现的 养老机构 用 these institutions 或 them 回指，避免与句首 institutions 重复，体现 衔接。 单复数与冠词 一系列标准 → a series of standards，standards 复数；service quality 作不可数概念不加 s。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: To improve the service quality of elderly care institutions, the government has issued a series of standards, strengthening the supervision of these institutions. 5. 许多城市为方便老年人用餐，开设了社区食堂，为他们提供价格实惠的饭菜。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 许多城市（主语）+ 开设（谓语）+ 社区食堂（宾语）（主语策略：原句主语） 主语是 许多城市 → Many cities；核心动作 开设了社区食堂 作主谓宾 have opened community canteens。为方便老年人用餐 是目的，为他们提供价格实惠的饭菜 是食堂的功能/结果，均降级 处理。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 一目的不定式 + 一功能定语从句 为方便老年人用餐 目的状语 to make dining more convenient for the elderly；为他们提供 价格实惠的饭菜 是食堂的功能，降级为定语从句 which provide affordable meals for them 修饰 canteens，避免再用 and 平排第三个动词。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 开设了 表已建成且仍在运营，用现在完成时 have opened；主语 Many cities 复数，用 have。 用词 价格实惠的 译 affordable（买得起的）最准，不要直译 cheap（含「廉价低质」贬义），这是用 词准确度的得分点。 单复数 社区食堂 多个城市各有，canteens 用复数；meals 也用复数。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: To make dining more convenient for the elderly, many cities have opened community canteens, which provide affordable meals for them. 6. 行动不便的老年人还能享受上门送餐服务。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 行动不便的老年人（主语）+ 能享受（谓语）+ 上门送餐服务（宾语）（主语策略：原句 主语） 主语是 行动不便的老年人 → elderly people with limited mobility；谓语宾语为 还能享受上门送 餐服务 → can also enjoy home meal delivery services。本句主谓宾齐全，是个相对完整的简 单句。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 「行动不便的」用后置介词短语作定语 行动不便的 修饰老年人，英文优先后置：with limited mobility / who have difficulty moving around 放在 elderly people 之后。上门送餐 译为 home delivery of meals / home meal delivery 作定语修饰 services。本句无多余动词，无需大改。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 本句讲常态服务，回指全篇一般现在时基调，用 can also enjoy，不必偏离。 单复数 行动不便的老年人 是一类人，elderly people 用复数；services / meals 用复数。 副词位置 还 表递进「除了堂食还能送上门」，用 also 放在 can 之后 enjoy 之前；同时为衔接上句，可在句 首加 In addition。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: In addition, elderly people with limited mobility can also enjoy home meal delivery services. 7. 同时，中国还在积极探索居家和社区养老等其他养老模式，以确保所有老年人老有所养。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 中国（主语）+ 探索（谓语）+ 其他养老模式（宾语）（主语策略：原句主语） 主语 中国 → China；核心动作 还在积极探索……其他养老模式 作主谓宾 is also actively exploring other elderly care models。以确保所有老年人老有所养 是目的，降级为 to ensure 不 定式。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 举例成分用 such as，目的用不定式 居家和社区养老等 是对「其他养老模式」的举例，用 such as home-based and community- based elderly care 插在 models 后；以确保所有老年人老有所养 降级为目的状语 to ensure that all the elderly are well cared for。注意「老有所养」意译，不可逐字。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 还在积极探索 的「还在」表此刻持续进行，用现在进行时 is exploring，与第2句的「正采取」同 类，是基调上的合理偏离。 四字格意译 老有所养 不可逐字译，意为「年老时得到妥善照料」→ all the elderly are well cared for / receive proper care in their old age。这是最考验是否懂「重表意而非对字」的地方。 单复数与连接 其他养老模式 不止一种，models 复数；居家和社区养老 两种并列用 and 连接 home-based and community-based。
